newsitem.title: CANADA: Princeton mine challenge heard by court.
newsitem.headline: Princeton mine challenge heard by court.

text.p: British Columbia Supreme Court is hearing this week arguments from native Indians who want permits for Princeton Mining Corp's Huckleberry copper mine to be cancelled, officials said Wednesday.
The native groups contend the British Columbia government violated its environmental assessment laws in approving the copper mine project in northern British Columbia.

Princeton is contesting the claims. Hearings were to end Thursday but Peter Campbell, Princeton environmental affairs manager, said as many as three more days may be needed. These may be rescheduled for a later date, he said.
The court is expected to reserve judgment after arguments are completed.

Four Japanese companies -- Marubeni Corp, Dowa Mining Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Materials Corp, Furukawa Co Ltd -- have 40 percent of the project and Princeton the rest. The Japanese firms will buy the entire production. Campbell said construction is running on schedule and production due to begin in September.
Copper output is forecast to average 65 million pounds a year during the first five years.
An application from the Cheslatta Carrier Nation to enjoin work on the project was rejected by the courts last summer.
